images.caption: Figure 1.The proposed framework includes four modules: (1) Energy modality-specific variational autoencoders that compress the energy map into compact latent tokens; (2) Two text encoders (CLIP and RemoteCLIP(Liu et al., 2024)) for embedding the static and dynamic prompts, respectively; (3) A U-ViT joint denoising network that models the joint distribution of all modalities via the self-attention mechanism; (4) Dynamic monthly energy consumption generation under static urban form.

Figure 2.Qualitative visualization of ground-truth and generated urban imagery and monthly energy consumption. The Energy changes are computed by the difference between monthly energy consumption values and the annual minimum values. Our generated monthly energy consumption and its trend are very similar to the ground truth.

Figure 3.Qualitative visualization of generated results across 4 cities. We sample some monthly generated energy results across seasons. (a) The comparison between GT and generated urban imagery and monthly building energy consumption maps in NYC. (b,c,d) Other cases in Washington, D.C., Busan, and Norfolk. The dynamic energy consumption trends are similar.
Figure 4.Generative augmentation effect on downstream building energy prediction metrics across different training set ratios.

Figure 5.Monthly energy consumption patterns generated by DySENSE across different cities. The curves compare the monthly mean energy consumption of generated maps and ground-truth maps. DySENSE captures seasonal and monthly dynamics well, with peak months exactly aligned with the ground truth in different cities.
Figure 6.Performance comparison on the downstream building energy consumption prediction task under different training-data strategies.
